subject: Re: Redwood private deployment — capacity commit & support tranches
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@silverlinehealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@silverlinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment economics & support options

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Procurement asked me to get a clearer read on your on‑prem/VPC pricing shape before our internal budget sync next Tuesday. Two specific asks:

1) We expect a steady baseline of ~8 p99 serving GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equiv) with occasional spikes to 12 for bursts. Can you provide a committed capacity SKU vs a burst/overage rate and the discount ladder for ~12/24/36 month commits?

2) How do you slice support? We need an SLA that includes 24/7 oncall for Sev1s, quarterly patch windows, and an option to buy additional L3 engineering hours in tranches. Also curious if platform fee is billed monthly vs annual and whether it can be waived/credited on a multi‑year commit.

If possible please send a simple pricing sheet and a redlineable SOW so our legal can start parallel review.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Director, Platform Procurement
Silverline Health

--
Attachment: none
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@silverlinehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment economics & support options

Hi Daniel — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Attached is a concise pricing sheet and a draft SOW to kick off procurement/legal review (see attachments). Key notes up front:

- Committed capacity SKUs: 8 GPU reserved, priced at a 28% discount off list if committed 12 months; 34% at 24 months; 40% at 36 months. Burst capacity billed at 1.8x per‑token rate after reserved throughput is exhausted.
- Platform fee: standard annual platform fee is 10% of committed capacity spend, invoiced quarterly. For commit >= 24 months we can offer a one‑time credit that effectively reduces the first year platform fee by 50%.
- Support tiers:
  * Standard: business hours (M‑F) support + monitoring dashboards
  * Premium: 24/7 Sev1 oncall + monthly health checks + two L3 support days/month
  * Premier: Premium + dedicated technical account manager + up to 40 L3 hours/year included
- L3 engineering hours: can be purchased in 40‑hour tranches at a discounted rate when bought with a committed capacity bundle.

I'll loop in finance and product for any adjustments; if you can confirm target commit term (12/24/36) and an expected PO/POE date, we can craft a final quote and optional redlines.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_VPC_Tiers_20261205.pdf; SOW-Silverline-v2.docx; Pricing-Schedule-SL-4591.xlsx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: internal: SL-4591 pricing flex

Stephanie — quick internal note before we finalize numbers for Silverline. A couple of levers we can use:

1) Platform fee credit: for 24+ month commits we can convert the 50% first‑year credit into an explicit "platform fee waiver" equal to one quarter of the platform fee paid up front (helps procurement signoff).
2) L3 tranche discount: take another 10% off L3 tranches if customer prepays for at least 80 hours (two tranches) in year one.
3) Burst cap: offer a capped burst budget (e.g., 20% of reserved monthly spend) where bursts are billed at 1.4x instead of 1.8x — this reduces billing surprises. This is contingent on commit >= 24 months.

If Silverline pushes for platform fee fully waived, product will need to confirm this doesn't create operational cost gaps — I'll check with infra. Grace, can you sanity‑check the burst cap proposal from an ops/SLO standpoint?

— Vivek
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: internal: SL-4591 pricing flex

Vivek — burst cap at 1.4x for up to 20% of monthly reserved spend is operationally acceptable if we:
- Require a 24‑month commit with a clearly defined rolling burn report;
- Include automatic throttling rules to protect p99 SLOs when usage exceeds burst cap;
- Add a quarterly usage review with Silverline to tune cache/batching.

If procurement agrees to the commit and quarterly reviews, ops can support the concession. I'll flag a small runbook addendum in the SOW about throttling behavior.

Grace
Senior Reliability PM
Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <dpark@silverlinehealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@silverlinehealth.com>, Silverline Legal <contracts@silverlinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment economics & support options

Stephanie — thanks for the detailed sheet. We discussed internally:

- We'll target a 24‑month commit with the expected baseline of 8 GPUs and a committed guarantee at that level.
- We like the burst cap idea, but need the burst budget to be explicitly listed in the SOW and capped at 20% as you suggested.
- On platform fee: procurement is asking for a full waiver of the first year platform fee in exchange for a signed 24‑month commitment and a PO within 10 business days. Is that something you can confirm?
- Finally, we need an estimated timeline for onboarding (install + validation), and a list of deliverables tied to milestones so we can align payment terms.

If you can send an updated SOW with the burst cap clause and the platform fee waiver option called out as a negotiable concession, we can move to PO.

Best,
Daniel
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@silverlinehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-07T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment economics & support options

Daniel — good news, we can accept the request with one condition: platform fee waived for year one in exchange for a signed 24‑month commit and PO within 10 business days, and a one‑time prepayment equal to one quarter of committed spend to cover onboarding/setup costs. We'll document the burst cap (20%) and the automatic throttling rules in Section 4.2 of the attached SOW.

Onboarding timeline (high level):
- Week 0: PO received + onboarding kickoff
- Weeks 1–2: environment readiness checks + provision control plane access
- Weeks 3–4: model onboarding, quantization tests, and perf tuning
- Week 5: validation run and handoff to ops

I'll attach the updated SOW (SOW‑Silverline‑v2.docx) and updated pricing schedule. If that looks good, please have procurement send PO to billing@redwood.ai and we'll spin up the kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
